Todd Achilles

Independent candidate for U.S. Senator, Idaho · Challenger

Public policy instructor at Boise State University; former technology executive and U.S. Army officer

Todd Achilles is a U.S. Army veteran and former technology executive from Boise. Gov. Brad Little appointed him to the Idaho House in February 2024, and he won the seat in November 2024 as a Democrat. He resigned in June 2025, registered as unaffiliated, and filed on February 26, 2026 to run for U.S. Senate as an independent.

Where Achilles stands

Cost of living and housing
Supports banning corporations from owning single-family homes and banning rent pricing set by algorithms, as part of a plan to make housing more affordable.
Energy prices
Says the Iran war is raising prices. He argues that Sen. Risch, as Foreign Relations chair, should hold public hearings on the war.
Iran war
Says the U.S. should be done with costly 'forever wars,' including the current war with Iran. Calls for congressional hearings and public accountability on the war.
Term limits and congressional ethics
Supports a constitutional amendment for term limits on Congress and the Supreme Court, a ban on members trading individual stocks, and a mandatory retirement age of 72 for Congress. He pledges to serve at most two terms.
Party caucus
Pledges not to caucus with either party if elected.
Public lands
Opposes selling Idaho's public lands, using the slogan 'Not One Damn Acre.'
Firearms
Says he will vote against new federal bans on firearms or magazines, a federal gun-owner registry, or any proposal that lacks due process protections.
Abortion
Says he will align his Senate service with the outcome of Idaho's reproductive freedom ballot initiative.
Medicaid and SNAP
Opposes the cuts to Medicaid and SNAP in federal budget legislation passed over the past year.

Background

  • U.S. Army armor officer and tank commander, 1992–1995
  • About 25 years in the technology sector (T-Mobile, Hewlett-Packard, startups)
  • Idaho House of Representatives, District 16B, 2024–2025 (appointed Feb 2024, elected Nov 2024); Minority Caucus Chair in 2025
  • Resigned from the Legislature on June 29, 2025, and announced an independent Senate run on July 1, 2025
  • Public policy instructor at Boise State University
  • B.A. in economics, Claremont McKenna College; graduate degrees in business, international studies, and public policy
  • Endorsed by the Forward Party (June 2026) and the American Federation of Government Employees (AFGE) (Sept 2026)
